Shield bearing Galactic Crusaders equipped with Melee weaponry for close in-engagements!

Five Armour Types, Segmented, Boarding, Plate, Ball-Bearing and Nu-Beaky.
10 Poses. Options for Radio and a Vexilla.
One pose, with the shield planted on the floor only worked with the blade guard shield, since the other is smaller.
Weapon options for Chainsword, Power Sword, Power Axe and Power fist,
Two shield types, one for a blade guard feel, and one more ornate older style.

Check out the "_standoffs" version. The models' feet are offset from the plug, allowing you to use the plug as a stand when painting, and then slice or snip off the small cylinders to allow you to glue the feet directly onto the base, for a seamless finish.

Thanks to Moonjammy, DangitBlobby and JimmyZimms for the base models, the Ball Bearing Armour and Beaky Armour, on which this is based.
A BIG thanks to LSTAR, who helped me with the export script for these guys. I wouldn't be able to put out the variety I have without it!

Thank you to MoonJam and Lord_Arner for many of the base parts!

Some Power Armoured Grey Knights for your Epic needs. These are scaled as 8mm marines like all of Moonjam's stuff. There are all the options needed for the current NetEA Developmental GK list. Everything for Strike Squads, Purgation Squads, Purifier Squads, Interceptor Squads, and even a little Crowe for good measure.

I have included supported .lys files for those who don't want the hassle of supporting them yourself. The supports are way more janky and not as nice as MoonJam's, but they do print. I have test printed them and they work.

Just a note, the painted models in the preview are from a previous version before purity seals were added. May the Emperor have mercy on your eyes when you are painting these.

These are largely based off of MoonJam's amazing Galactic Crusaders. I also took the helmets from Lord_Arner's Daybreak Strikers. There is also a Plaguebearer head for which I cannot find the link from jimjimjimmyjim in there so thanks to him as well. A few bits were my own design but the credit should really be theirs.
